items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: I think it was Bill Cray, somebody like that, or Leonard Ferguson

ctx.x: Well, I think the foundation of a band? Drum, bass, and piano. That's your foundation. That's what gives it its depth.

I don't know. I think it was Bill Cray, somebody like that, or Leonard Ferguson, one of the guys, musicians that I've talked to, saying that all nightclub owners want to get rid of bass. They don't understand the importance of it, you know. No, I don't. And he was saying how important the bass is.

I don't agree with that. Not all nightclubers want to. I'll tell you where you might have misunderstood them. It's not the nightclub owners want to get rid of the bass. It's because to a band leader, your drum, bass, and piano are three important instruments. You're a foundation. We're supplying the bottom, and we're giving it the drive and the depth.
